Iteration 1/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: No prior claims or evidence exist, so the first step is to register well-powered, mechanistically motivated comparisons. I prioritize binary predictors whose exposed and comparator groups are both well above the required minimum cell size. The registered hypotheses cover four complementary biological themes: driver-gene dependency, including KRAS, EGFR amplification, ERBB2 amplification, BRAF V600E, and the RAS-pathway paralog RIT1; p53-axis dependency, including expected reduced MDM2 and USP7 dependency after TP53 loss; selective synthetic lethality or paralog dependency, including WRN in MSI-high cells and SMARCA2 in SMARCA4-loss cells; and MYC-associated transcriptional/translational stress, using MYC amplification as a marker for MYC-driven dependence on DHX9 and RPL11, plus the NRF2-axis comparison of KEAP1 loss and NFE2L2 dependency. The direction field encodes the claim being tested: direction -1 corresponds to a lower dependency score, meaning stronger dependency, while direction +1 corresponds to a higher dependency score, meaning weaker dependency. Anticipated_direction is my expected raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence. These are associative hypotheses in this dataset and should not be interpreted as causal until effect sizes, uncertainty, and validation support them. I defer rare subgroup interactions and continuous dichotomized assays until direct effects are estimated and cell sizes are verified.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative:
The discovery batch produced three unambiguous, large associations in the claimed direction. H1 shows MSI-high cells have much stronger WRN dependency; H2 shows SMARCA4-loss cells have much stronger SMARCA2 dependency; H10 shows TP53-loss cells have much weaker USP7 dependency. The signed intervals are far from zero and, converted to raw exposed-minus-comparator differences, the effects are roughly -0.79, -0.78, and +0.40 dependency-score units respectively. These are not just statistically large; relative to comparator means they are well above the 10% clinical-significance benchmark. I therefore accept H1, H2, and H10 for this dataset, while retaining them as active for robustness follow-up rather than claiming causality or cross-cohort generalizability.

The MYC-amplification comparisons H8 and H12 are null and tiny. The direct driver-gene hypotheses are mostly null or tiny: H4 KRAS-mutation/KRAS dependency is about a 6% relative difference with an interval crossing zero; H6 ERBB2 amplification/ERBB2 dependency is essentially zero; H7 BRAF V600E/BRAF dependency points slightly opposite but is small; H9 RIT1/KRAS-mutation is tiny; H3 TP53-loss/MDM2 dependency is only about 3% relative, despite a prior biological expectation. I reject these as unsupported in this dataset. H5 EGFR-amplification/EGFR dependency is the only borderline case: the point estimate is about a 10.2% relative stronger dependency, but the 95% interval includes zero. I leave H5 unresolved and request independent validation for it because a validation result would directly determine whether this borderline EGFR signal is worth adding to the accepted set.

H11 is important as an anti-hypothesis finding. The original claim expected KEAP1 loss to strengthen NFE2L2 dependency, but the signed estimate is strongly negative, meaning the raw contrast is large and positive: KEAP1-loss cells show weaker NFE2L2 dependency score, roughly +0.80 relative to comparator and over 300% relative to the comparator mean. This rejects H11 as originally specified. Rather than discard the signal, I registered a reversed follow-up claim with parent H11 so the opposite association can be assessed under a directionally correct hypothesis. I also registered adenocarcinoma-restricted robustness follow-ups for the three accepted large effects and one KRAS co-loss follow-up to test whether the KRAS direct null hides context-specific effects. No validation was requested for the large accepted effects because internal evidence is already decisive; H5 is the most decision-relevant uncertain claim.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];

evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional

plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative:
Synthesis report. Validation response deadline assessed for H5. The independent validation for EGFR amplification versus EGFR dependency is in the same signed direction as the borderline discovery estimate but smaller and imprecise. Discovery raw exposed-minus-comparator difference was about -0.025, roughly a 10 percent stronger dependency, with a 95 percent interval crossing zero. Validation raw difference was about -0.015, roughly 6 percent, and the independent interval includes zero, small opposite effects, and clinically meaningful effects. Therefore I do not upgrade H5 to accept. I also do not reject it as a true null because the interval remains wide; I record it as unresolved with investigation deferred. If future evidence is sought, a larger independent replication or a pre-specified adjusted/model estimate would be more informative than repeated post-hoc subgroup mining.

I reassess H13 and accept it. The evidence R11 for KEAP1 loss and NFE2L2 dependency is directionally strong under the reversed claim: raw contrast about +0.80, meaning weaker NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-loss cells, with a very tight interval. The original hypothesis H11, which expected stronger dependency, was correctly rejected as unsupported; the reversed claim H13 is now supported.

Supported findings in this dataset, all associative and not causal: MSI-high cells show much stronger WRN dependency; SMARCA4-loss cells show much stronger SMARCA2 dependency; TP53-loss cells show much weaker USP7 dependency; KEAP1-loss cells show much weaker NFE2L2 dependency. These raw differences are around 0.78 to 0.80 dependency-score units for the first two and KEAP1/NFE2L2, or about 300 percent relative to comparator means, and about 0.40 for USP7, roughly 150 percent relative to comparator. All clear the 10 percent clinical-significance benchmark and have intervals far from zero.

Negative or null findings: direct KRAS mutation versus KRAS dependency, EGFR amplification versus EGFR dependency at the accepted level, ERBB2 amplification versus ERBB2 dependency, BRAF V600E versus BRAF dependency, KRAS mutation versus RIT1 dependency, TP53 loss versus MDM2 dependency, MYC amplification versus DHX9 or RPL11 dependency, and the original KEAP1-loss versus NFE2L2 stronger-dependency hypothesis were not supported. The driver-gene tests are especially useful because they show that strong associations are not a generic consequence of driver-status labels in this dataset. The MYC tests argue against broad DHX9 or RPL11 dependency effects from MYC amplification. The original KEAP1 anti-hypothesis was not just null but strongly opposite, and the reversed claim was accepted.

Unresolved uncertainty: H5 remains the main borderline case. Existing robustness claims H14 through H16 test accepted effects in adenocarcinoma, and H17 tests whether the KRAS-null effect is hidden in a TP53-loss context. Newly registered H18 tests the KEAP1/NFE2L2 reversed association in adenocarcinoma. H19 tests the SMARCA4/SMARCA2 association within ARID1A-wild-type cells to probe SWI/SNF context and co-mutation specificity. H20 tests MYC amplification against USP7 dependency as a biologically motivated follow-up to USP7 pathway effects, and H21 uses POLR2A versus MSI-high as a specificity control. These analyses should first establish internal generalizability and specificity before broader interpretation.

Limitations: all samples are lung lineage, with most adenocarcinoma, so findings are limited to this dataset. Screen batch, CRISPR library, Cas9 activity, ploidy, aneuploidy, co-mutation structure, and media conditions could confound associations. The accepted effects are large enough to be unlikely to be purely trivial, but causal direction and external generalizability remain unproven. Next priority is to execute the pre-planned robustness and specificity analyses and stop EGFR work unless an independent replication is possible.

  "narrative": "This exploration adds targeted follow-up to the first round. First, I refine the rejected KRAS-mutation/KRAS-dependency claim by testing the effect only among BRAF wild-type cells; if BRAF mutant cells bypass KRAS, a restriction may reveal a KRAS-mutation association that is otherwise diluted. Second, I test downstream pathway-bypass hypotheses: activating PIK3CA mutation and PTEN loss should increase PI3K signaling and therefore weaken upstream EGFR or ERBB2 dependency, meaning a higher dependency score and direction +1. The alternative is no effect if these are merely co-drivers rather than dominant bypass mechanisms. Third, I test transcriptional addiction: MYC amplification should increase dependency on POLR2A, the core RNA polymerase II subunit, with stronger dependency expected as a lower dependency score and direction -1. Fourth, I extend receptor tyrosine kinase signaling to STAT3: EGFR or ERBB2 amplification may activate STAT3 and create stronger STAT3 dependency, direction -1. record.narrative: This exploration adds targeted follow-up to the first round. First, I refine the rejected KRAS-mutation/KRAS-dependency claim by testing the effect only among BRAF wild-type cells; if BRAF mutant cells bypass KRAS, a restriction may reveal a KRAS-mutation association that is otherwise diluted. Second, I test downstream pathway-bypass hypotheses: activating PIK3CA mutation and PTEN loss should increase PI3K signaling and therefore weaken upstream EGFR or ERBB2 dependency, meaning a higher dependency score and direction +1. The alternative is no effect if these are merely co-drivers rather than dominant bypass mechanisms. Third, I test transcriptional addiction: MYC amplification should increase dependency on POLR2A, the core RNA polymerase II subunit, with stronger dependency expected as a lower dependency score and direction -1. Fourth, I extend receptor tyrosine kinase signaling to STAT3: EGFR or ERBB2 amplification may activate STAT3 and create stronger STAT3 dependency, direction -1. Fifth, I probe specificity of the accepted effects. ARID1A loss is a related SWI/SNF chromatin-remodeling alteration, and if SMARCA2 dependency is a broader SWI/SNF vulnerability, it should show the same stronger-dependency direction as SMARCA4 loss; if not, the SMARCA4 effect is more context-specific. BRCA2 loss is used as a DNA-repair specificity control for the MSI-high/WRN effect: a null BRCA2 association would support MMR-specific WRN dependency rather than a generic DNA-repair deficiency effect. Finally, I add robustness and co-mutation context for the accepted large effects by testing the SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 and KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 effects within TP53-loss cells, and by testing the MSI-high/WRN effect within Avana-library cells to assess whether library effects could confound the association. These are associative dataset claims; acceptance will require 95% intervals that exclude zero and an effect size that clears the 10% relative clinical-significance benchmark. No new validation is requested yet because no new evidence has been produced, and H5 remains deferred unresolved.

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

First, I refine the rejected KRAS-mutation/KRAS-dependency claim by testing the effect only among BRAF wild-type cells; if BRAF mutant cells bypass KRAS, a restriction may reveal a KRAS-mutation association that is otherwise diluted. Second, I test downstream pathway-bypass hypotheses: activating PIK3CA mutation and PTEN loss should increase PI3K signaling and therefore weaken upstream EGFR or ERBB2 dependency, meaning a higher dependency score and direction +1. The alternative is no effect if these are merely co-drivers rather than dominant bypass mechanisms. Third, I test transcriptional addiction: MYC amplification should increase dependency on POLR2A, the core RNA polymerase II subunit, with stronger dependency expected as a lower dependency score and direction -1. Fourth, I extend receptor tyrosine kinase signaling to STAT3: EGFR or ERBB2 amplification may activate STAT3 and create stronger STAT3 dependency, direction -1. Fifth, I probe specificity of the accepted effects. ARID1A loss is a related SWI/SNF chromatin-remodeling alteration, and if SMARCA2 dependency is a broader SWI/SNF vulnerability, it should show the same stronger-dependency direction as SMARCA4 loss; if not, the SMARCA4 effect is more context-specific. BRCA2 loss is used as a DNA-repair specificity control for the MSI-high/WRN effect: a null BRCA2 association would support MMR-specific WRN dependency rather than a generic DNA-repair deficiency effect. Finally, I add robustness and co-mutation context for the accepted large effects by testing the SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 and KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 effects within TP53-loss cells, and by testing the MSI-high/WRN effect within Avana-library cells to assess whether library effects could confound the association. H33 tests MSI-high WRN dependency within Avana-library cells to assess possible CRISPR library confounding. H31 and H32 test whether the SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 and KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 associations persist within TP53-loss cells, probing co-mutation structure and potential epistatic context. Specificity controls include H29, which asks whether ARID1A loss is also associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency as a broader SWI/SNF predictor; H30, which asks whether BRCA2 loss is associated with WRN dependency as a DNA-repair deficiency control; and H21, which asks whether MSI-high is associated with POLR2A dependency as a transcriptional specificity control for the MSI/WRN signal. H22 refines the null KRAS direct test by asking whether KRAS mutation associates with stronger KRAS dependency after excluding BRAF V600E cells, where BRAF mutant cells might bypass KRAS dependency. The signed intervals are far from zero and, converted to raw exposed-minus-comparator differences, the effects are roughly -0.79, -0.78, and +0.40 dependency-score units respectively. These are not just statistically large; relative to comparator means they are well above the 10% clinical-significance benchmark. I therefore accept H1, H2, and H10 for this dataset, while retaining them as active for robustness follow-up rather than claiming causality or cross-cohort generalizability.\n\nThe MYC-amplification comparisons H8 and H12 are null and tiny. I reject these as unsupported in this dataset. H5 EGFR-amplification/EGFR dependency is the only borderline case: the point estimate is about a 10.2% relative stronger dependency, but the 95% interval includes zero. I leave H5 unresolved and request independent validation for it because a validation result would directly determine whether this borderline EGFR signal is worth adding to the accepted set.\n\nH11 is important as an anti-hypothesis finding. This rejects H11 as originally specified. Rather than discard the signal, I registered a reversed follow-up claim with parent H11 so the opposite association can be assessed under a directionally correct hypothesis. I also registered adenocarcinoma-restricted robustness follow-ups for the three accepted large effects and one KRAS co-loss follow-up to test whether the KRAS direct null hides context-specific effects. record.narrative: This batch delivers strong internal robustness for the main accepted associations. H14, H15, H16, H18, H31, H32, and H33 all have signed 95% intervals far from zero in the claimed direction. Because positive signed estimates for direction -1 correspond to raw negative exposed-minus-comparator differences, the WRN and SMARCA2 effects remain much stronger dependency; because positive signed estimates for direction +1 correspond to raw positive differences, the USP7 and NFE2L2 effects remain much weaker dependency. The magnitudes are roughly 0.78 to 0.81 units for WRN/SMARCA2/NFE2L2 and about 0.39 to 0.41 units for USP7, all far above the 10% relative benchmark after accounting for comparator means. I therefore accept these subgroup/eligibility comparisons as supported dataset-associative findings and keep them active because they are robustness/context checks, not external validation. H33 in the Avana library subset makes library confounding less likely for the MSI-high/WRN effect, though it does not establish the effect in the smaller non-Avana subset. H31 and H32 show persistence within TP53-loss co-mutation contexts despite smaller exposed cells, but co-mutation correlation could still partially explain or modify these associations. The specificity controls and pathway refinements are not supported. H29: ARID1A loss is not associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency; the point estimate is small and actually opposite the expected direction. H30: BRCA2 loss shows no WRN-dependency signal, supporting that the accepted WRN association is more MSI/MMR-related than a generic DNA-repair-label effect, although a non-significant control does not prove absence. H21: MSI-high is not associated with POLR2A dependency, supporting specificity of the MSI/WRN signal. H22: KRAS mutation still does not show a scientifically meaningful association with KRAS dependency among BRAF wild-type cells; the point is near the null and the interval includes zero. H25: PTEN loss is not associated with weaker EGFR dependency in the expected direction; the small interval excludes a meaningful positive signal. These nulls reduce the chance that every large result is a generic driver-label artifact, but they remain associative and non-causal. I do not request independent validation now: the newly supported effects are internally large and precise, and the main borderline EGFR claim H5 has already been independently probed and remains unresolved/deferred. Future value lies in completing targeted co-mutation, technical, and pathway checks rather than repeating large accepted contrasts.

record.narrative:
No new validation evidence has arrived since the H5 response; H5 is the only validation released, and it does not change the conclusion. I reassess H5 as unresolved but close the EGFR amplification investigation because the independent estimate is small and imprecise, and additional post-hoc EGFR subgrouping would be low-value unless a larger independent replication or adjusted model is available.

Supported findings in this dataset are associative, not causal, and remain limited to lung lineage with adenocarcinoma dominance. MSI-high cells show much stronger WRN dependency (H1; internally robust in adenocarcinoma H14 and Avana-library cells H33). SMARCA4-loss cells show much stronger SMARCA2 dependency (H2; robust in adenocarcinoma H15 and TP53-loss context H31). TP53-loss cells show much weaker USP7 dependency (H10; robust in adenocarcinoma H16). KEAP1-loss cells show much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, the reversed direction of H11 (H13; robust in adenocarcinoma H18 and TP53-loss context H32). These raw contrasts are on the order of 0.39-0.80 dependency-score units and their signed 95% intervals exclude zero with substantial margins. They clear the 10% relative-difference benchmark comfortably; they are far too large to be interpreted as small dataset artifacts without a separate mechanism, but they are still only within-dataset associations.

Negative or unsupported comparisons include the direct driver-gene tests H3 (TP53 loss/MDM2), H4 and H22 (KRAS mutation/KRAS dependency overall and excluding BRAF), H6 (ERBB2 amplification/ERBB2 dependency), H7 (BRAF V600E/BRAF dependency), H8 and H12 (MYC amplification/DHX9 and RPL11), H9 (KRAS mutation/RIT1), H25 (PTEN loss/EGFR), H29 (ARID1A loss/SMARCA2), H30 (BRCA2 loss/WRN), and H21 (MSI-high/POLR2A). These are informative because they reduce the likelihood that large associations are generic driver-label effects; however, they do not prove absence or exclude effect modification.

Unresolved uncertainty remains for H5. The discovery estimate was borderline near the 10% relative benchmark, while independent validation was smaller (~6% relative) with an interval that includes zero, opposite effects, and clinically meaningful effects. No claim of generalizability is made for any effect. Confounding by co-mutation structure, screen batch/library, Cas9 quality, ploidy/aneuploidy, media, and multiple testing remains possible.

The most informative next analyses are the pending pathway and specificity claims H17-H28 plus newly registered context and covariate robustness tests. The new proposals ask whether accepted effects persist in important co-mutation contexts (ARID1A-wild-type for SMARCA4/SMARCA2; TP53-wild-type for KEAP1/NFE2L2; KEAP1-loss for TP53/USP7; SMARCA4-loss for KEAP1/NFE2L2) and under median-split aneuploidy, ploidy, and screen-quality conditions, and they include two arbitrary research-marker negative controls. I prioritize completing these before broad biological interpretation or additional EGFR work.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: No assessments are due. I am requesting 12 untested claims to maximize new scientific information without rerunning previously compared cells. Priority is given to (1) context-specific robustness of the four large accepted associations, (2) formal interaction tests of whether these associations are modified by genomic-structural or screen-quality variables, (3) direct MYC amplification hypotheses that can reveal additional predictors, and (4) arbitrary marker negative controls for the accepted USP7/NFE2L2 associations. H34 tests whether SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 dependency persists when ARID1A is wild-type, which is important because ARID1A loss itself was not predictive in H29. H35 tests KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 dependency in TP53-wild-type cells, complementing H32 and probing whether the very large KEAP1 effect requires TP53-loss context. H36 tests TP53-loss/USP7 dependency within KEAP1-loss cells, another co-mutation specificity check. H43 and H44 ask whether the MSI-high/WRN association is modified by aneuploidy or screen quality, respectively; these test biological genomic-instability dependence versus technical assay confounding. H45 asks whether SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 dependency varies with ploidy, H46 asks whether KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 dependency varies with TP53 loss, and H47 asks whether TP53-loss/USP7 dependency varies with MYC amplification. These interactions are more informative than simple strata for identifying subgroup-specific effects. H20 tests MYC amplification directly with USP7 dependency, complementing H47 by distinguishing a direct MYC association from modification of the TP53-loss effect. H48 tests MYC amplification with MDM2 dependency, a plausible proliferative p53-pathway stress hypothesis. H52 and H53 are negative-control tests using arbitrary marker F against USP7 and NFE2L2 dependency; null results would strengthen the interpretation that the accepted TP53/USP7 and KEAP1/NFE2L2 associations are label-specific rather than generic constructed-assay artifacts. All claims are still within-dataset associations; no causal or generalizability inference will be drawn.
